questions.question: What can happen if you take a turn too fast?

options.text: It is safe as long as you stay under the speed limit.
It is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
It is safe as long as no other vehicles are near you.
You may end up in another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may end up in another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. If you cannot control the turn, you may drift into another lane or go off the road. Always slow down when turning.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider improve their visibility?
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials to be seen by other drivers. Also use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: When should you do a complete check of your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle completely before every ride. Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time can reduce your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change how alcohol affects you.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What should you check during a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluids, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: How often should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Inspect your motorcycle before every ride. It only takes a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you ride in traffic.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit and other regulatory signs are rectangular and white with black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Any time you plan to change lanes.
Only when it is dark outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to impair your riding?

options.text: At about half the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. You can be impaired before reaching the legal limit. Do not drink any alcohol before riding.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials at night to help other drivers see you. Bright colors with reflective materials make you more visible.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: You don't need a head check if you use your mirrors.
Your mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Assume other drivers will see your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is an important reason to wear a leather jacket when riding?

options.text: It's too warm to wear in hot weather.
It protects you in a crash.
You should not wear one when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, preferably leather, when riding. Leather jackets protect you in a crash and can help keep you cool in hot weather.

questions.question: Which of these checks do you NOT need to do before riding?

options.text: Test both brakes to make sure the brake light works.
Check that the paint is not scratched.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the paint is not scratched.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire pressure and condition, oil and fluid levels, and that all lights work (headlight, taillight, signal lights, and brake light).

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing and gear. This makes it easier for other drivers to see you and your motorcycle.

questions.question: Which color helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, yellow, or green clothing. These colors make you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see and be seen.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see and be seen.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to help you see others and be seen. It should also help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. A good lane position discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What is it called when you shift to a lower gear?
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to braking. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, what should you be ready for?

options.text: A car suddenly pulling out into traffic.
Other drivers noticing you and staying out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car suddenly pulling out into traffic.
questions.explanation: Be prepared for a parked car to suddenly move into traffic. It is safest to ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on the right. This gives you more space between your motorcycle and any danger.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes when needed, slow down, and avoid sudden moves. Watch out for oil, shaded areas, dirt, gravel, and bridges—these surfaces have less grip.

questions.question: Who is most likely to have a crash?

options.text: Riders who completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Beginning riders who are untrained and unfamiliar with their motorcycle have the most crashes.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either brake, but never both together.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time. Using both brakes together stops you most effectively.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may make them tailgate you even closer.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
The faster your body removes the alcohol.
The less effect the alcohol has on you.
The more likely you will avoid being pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the more alcohol builds up in your body. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Can a motorcycle share a lane with a car?

options.text: Yes, if there is enough room.
No, a motorcycle needs a full lane to operate safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, a motorcycle needs a full lane to operate safely.
questions.explanation: Both motorcycles and cars need the full width of a lane to operate safely. They should never share a lane.
